香典 こうでん — condolence money; funeral gift

香典 is a condolence gift offered in connection with a funeral, usually money. It names the offering, not the funeral ceremony or incense itself. The dictionary definition also allows goods; "money" is a practical translation, not an absolute restriction.
香典を用意しました。 (こうでんをよういしました。) — I prepared condolence money.
香典を渡しました。 (こうでんをわたしました。) — I handed over the condolence money.
In both examples, を marks the gift as the object. 用意する (よういする) means "prepare"; 渡す (わたす) means "hand over."

香 supplies the incense connection; 典 also occurs in ceremonial vocabulary. Learn this as an established funeral-offering compound, not a freely productive formula: 典 alone does not mean "money." The on readings コウ + デン give こうでん.
The same word is also written 香奠 (こうでん). JMdict marks that alternate spelling as rare; the flag does not make the pronunciation こうでん rare.

贈り物 (おくりもの) and プレゼント mean a gift more generally, without specifying a funeral. 寄付 (きふ) is a donation or contribution, not specifically a funeral condolence gift. お祝い (おいわい), a celebration or congratulatory gift, concerns a happy occasion instead. There is no single useful lexical opposite.

Use the whole word for the funeral-related offering. Do not translate it as an ordinary birthday present, the funeral itself, or a stick of incense. The word does not tell you an appropriate amount or every community's customs; this is vocabulary guidance, not an etiquette prescription.
